Cc: Alex Park <alex.park@medgenix.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps for evaluation / contracting

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited and wants to lock a practical close timeline so we can schedule procurement and data-security reviews on our side. Two asks from procurement/legal: a one-page sequencing plan that shows the order we need MSA, DPA, and order form signed, and a short list of acceptance criteria for the pilot (so we can map internal UAT/resourcing).

Can Redwood share a recommended sequence and a proposed staggered onramp approach? Ideally we want to avoid blocking the PSA team (they require MSA/DPA before any sandbox access) but procurement has asked if we can do a conditional pilot signature for the order form contingent on DPA controls being met.

If you send a simple mutual action plan and a proposed acceptance checklist this week, I can push internal legal and procurement to a decision the following week.

Best,
Priya
Priya Sharma
Director, Platform Integrations — MedGenix

From: irene_choi@redwood.com

Cc: Alex Park <alex.park@medgenix.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sequencing proposal: staggered onramp + MSA/DPA/order form cadence for MedGenix

Hi Priya — thanks for laying out procurement's constraints.

Quick answer up front: yes, we can support a staggered onramp that unblocks engineering work while legal finalizes the DPA. Proposed high-level sequence below (we'll attach a one-page MAP + acceptance checklist after sync):

- Step 0: NDA / Confidentiality already in place (confirmed)
- Step 1: Sign MSA with core commercial terms and order form scope (redlines tolerated, but commercial terms agreed) — this enables billing and executive approval lanes.
- Step 2 (parallel): Redwood provides the DPA draft and the completed security questionnaire; MedGenix legal runs the review. We accept a targeted carve for data residency in the DPA if the pilot uses pseudonymized data.
- Step 3: Conditional pilot order form signature (sandbox access) — this is a limited-order form that is explicitly contingent on DPA completion and security gating before production. It gives your teams access to the sandbox and a small token commit for resources.
- Step 4: Acceptance run (2–4 weeks) using the attached acceptance tests doc; tech success gates mapped to rollback conditions.
- Step 5: Post-acceptance: sign full production order form and confirm DPA / final clause for data residency & retention.

We think this preserves procurement's need to see a signed order form to allocate budget while keeping production gated behind the DPA. I'll circulate a 1-page MAP and an acceptance checklist (with instrumentation & SLOs) by EOD.

Action: karthik, can you help confirm that our engineering team can enable sandbox access on signing of the conditional order form, and attach the acceptance tests we intend to use?

Thanks — Irene Choi
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_MAP_draft_v2.pdf (stub)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 09:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sequencing proposal: staggered onramp + MSA/DPA/order form cadence for MedGenix

Irene / Marissa — looping in procurement lead (Neha) for sequencing constraints. Internal notes below (keeping language we can share with the customer):

- Engineering: we can provision a sandbox cluster within 48 hours of a signed conditional order form. The sandbox will have limited tokens and a pseudonymized dataset flag. We'll require a signed AUP and a short SOC2 access addendum for audit access.
- Legal: MSA + Order form first, DPA parallel review. If MedGenix must have DPA signed before any MSA signature, we can reverse but that will delay sandbox by ~7–10 business days.
- Commercial: recommend the conditional order form include a 30-day trial credit and an explicit clause that full production billing will not trigger until DPA is executed.

Marissa — can you prepare the conditional order form language (bullet points) and the acceptance-test matrix? I'll attach the security QA responses and highlight areas we expect negotiation: data residency, subprocessor list, and logging retention.

-karthik
Senior Director, Deal Operations

Attachment: proposed-acceptance-tests.md (stub); MedGenix_Security_QA_Responses.xlsx (stub)

Thanks — this looks workable. Two points from Procurement/Legal:

1) Procurement wants the conditional language stuck into the order form (clear bullets on what "conditional" means: sandbox-only access, token caps, no production data processing).
2) Legal asks that the DPA include a clause about subprocessors and that Redwood provide an interim SOC2 attestation while the final DPA is negotiated.

We can accept the workflow you proposed if Redwood provides the interim SOC2 attestation and confirms the subprocessor list now. If you can send the conditional order form language and the one-page MAP by EOD Monday, I'll escalate to procurement for an internal deadline of next Thursday (31 Jul).

Best,
Priya

Hi Priya — attaching the one-page MAP (summary) and the conditional order form bullets per your ask. Small clarifications inline:

- Conditional order form bullets (summary):
  * Access: sandbox-only environment; tenant isolated; maximum 100k tokens/month during pilot.
  * Billing: $0 - credit-backed pilot; production billing only starts after DPA fully executed and production order form signed.
  * Data: sandbox to use pseudonymized or synthetic records only; no PHI allowed in sandbox.
  * Duration: 30-day pilot with two-week acceptance testing window.
  * Termination: immediate suspension if security gating conditions fail.

- Interim compliance: Redwood will provide our latest SOC2 Type II attestation (dated 2025-05) and a current subprocessor list (attached).

Next steps: if you confirm the acceptance test matrix (attached) we'll push DocuSign for the conditional order form and MSA signature lanes next week.

Thanks — Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference
